title: Moral Development (Kohlberg)
summary: Kohlberg's theory: three levels of moral development (preconventional, conventional, postconventional), each with two stages, based on moral reasoning about dilemmas.
objectives: Describe Kohlberg's three levels of moral development.
Identify the basis of reasoning at each level.
revision: Kohlberg's moral development: three levels (preconventional, conventional, postconventional).

notes.t: The development of moral reasoning and ethical judgment across the lifespan.

r: Stage 3: Interpersonal accord; Stage 4: Authority/social order
Stage 5: Social contract; Stage 6: Universal principles

notes.t: Moral development progresses through invariant sequences; not everyone reaches postconventional reasoning.
UGC NET frequently asks about Kohlberg's three levels and Heinz dilemma.

mnemonics.title: CPP
mnemonics.text: C — Preconventional (punishment/reward), C — Conventional (approval/rules), P — Postconventional (principles/justice)
